title: Remove Duplicates from Unsorted Linked List
description:
Given the `head` of an unsorted singly linked list, remove duplicate nodes so that only the **first occurrence** of each distinct value remains in the list, preserving the original relative order of the kept nodes.

Return the head of the modified linked list.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Maintain a hash set of values already seen while traversing the list with `prev` and `curr` pointers.
Whenever `curr.val` is already in the set, unlink `curr` via `prev.next = curr.next`; otherwise add `curr.val` to the set and advance `prev = curr`.

examples.explanation: Keeping the first occurrence of each value in [3, 1, 2, 1, 3, 4] yields [3, 1, 2, 4].
Every node has value 5, so only the first node [5] is kept.
All values in [4, -1, 7, 0] are already distinct, so the list is unchanged.
